title: When the Sea Turns Cold, Rescuers Rush to Save Sea Turtles
summary:
On a dark, chilly December afternoon in 2025, volunteer Annemarie O'Connell drove to a beach in Truro, Massachusetts, near the tip of Cape Cod, with a flashlight in hand. She was looking for sea turtles that had washed ashore, too cold to swim.

Like other reptiles, most sea turtles cannot make their own body heat. They stay comfortable in water between about 17 and 29 degrees Celsius (62 to 85 degrees Fahrenheit). In summer, warming seas draw many turtles north. In fall and winter, they head back south toward the tropics.

But if the water drops below 10 degrees Celsius (50 degrees Fahrenheit) before they move on, turtles can get too cold. They weaken and slow down, with less energy to dive and feed. It is also harder for their bodies to fight off infections. Some stop swimming and drift at the surface. This condition, called cold stunning, leaves turtles dazed and numb.

Every winter, hundreds of cold-stunned turtles wash up on Massachusetts beaches. Many had been swimming south but could not get beyond Cape Cod. Cold stunning is also a problem along Gulf and Pacific coasts, where shallow water along Florida and Texas can chill quickly during cold snaps.

Government workers and conservation groups patrol beaches in late fall and winter, looking for cold-stunned turtles. Without help, these animals may die. But if they are moved quickly to special hospitals, many will survive. That is what brought O'Connell to the beach. Around high tide, she found a large loggerhead about one meter (three feet) long. 'It was huge,' she remembers, 'like a rock that had plopped out of the sky.' Its eyes were swollen shut, but when she approached, it moved its head. Helpers slid it onto a sled and drove it toward care.
why_it_matters: Warming seas draw many turtles north in summer, so a sudden drop in water temperature can leave them stranded far from the warm water they need. Quick rescue matters because, without help, cold-stunned turtles may die, while many survive if they reach special hospitals in time.

questions.question: Why can sea turtles become cold-stunned in fall and winter?
options: They stop eating in summer and run out of energy.
They prefer cold water and swim north to find it.
They cannot make their own body heat, and water below 10 degrees Celsius (50 degrees Fahrenheit) can leave them too cold to swim.
Their shells crack when the air turns chilly.
questions.correct_answer: They cannot make their own body heat, and water below 10 degrees Celsius (50 degrees Fahrenheit) can leave them too cold to swim.

questions.question: In what water temperatures do most sea turtles stay comfortable?
options: Between about 17 and 29 degrees Celsius (62 to 85 degrees Fahrenheit)
Below 10 degrees Celsius
Above 40 degrees Celsius
Only in water at exactly 10 degrees Celsius
questions.correct_answer: Between about 17 and 29 degrees Celsius (62 to 85 degrees Fahrenheit)

background_read: Sea turtles are reptiles that cannot make their own body heat, so they depend on warm water to stay active and healthy.
In summer, warming seas draw many turtles north, and in fall and winter they head back south toward warmer waters.
If the water around them cools too much before they move on, they can become cold-stunned, growing weak, slow, and unable to dive or feed well.
People who patrol beaches in the cold months look for these stranded turtles and bring them to special hospitals where many can recover.
